public_source_observations.stock_task_gap: RunAsTaskAsync still durably awaits CreateTaskAsync before volatile Task.Run; the create-new/unique-ID task-store contract has no start-existing/redrive claim.
public_source_observations.ordinary_pipeline: McpRequestFilters documents ordinary CallToolFilters as running inside the alternate-result pipeline, and for task-backed calls they execute in the background after task creation and before the matched tool.
public_source_observations.primitive_entrypoint: McpServerTool exposes public InvokeAsync(RequestContext<CallToolRequestParams>, ...), but this is the primitive tool invocation, not a documented replay entrypoint for the complete call-tool middleware/filter pipeline.
public_source_observations.full_replacement_handler: McpServerHandlers.CallToolWithAlternateHandler is documented as a low-level full replacement and cannot be composed with ordinary CallToolFilters.
public_source_observations.task_server_binding: Current WithTasks creates a new RequestContext for background work but preserves MatchedPrimitive/services and replaces executionRequest.Server with a task-aware interceptor derived from the original request.Server. This is process/request-context state, not a durable restart envelope.

requirements: Atomically persist the new task and an immutable replayable invocation/outbox before acknowledging task creation.
Use a durable claim with monotonic attempt generation so only one live dispatcher owns an attempt and stale attempts cannot record terminal state.
After claim expiry/takeover, reconstruct the full ordinary call-tool policy/filter pipeline, not only McpServerTool.InvokeAsync.
Revalidate or cryptographically bind principal/authorization context; fail closed when user-delegated authority or required client/session context cannot be safely reconstructed.
CAS completion/cancellation against the exact attempt generation.
Use effect-side stable idempotency or an atomic effect-generation fence for non-idempotent external effects because a lease can expire while an old attempt is inside the effect.
candidate_contract.api_consequence: A conforming fix cannot be implemented only by changing IMcpTaskStore.CreateTaskAsync behavior to return an existing task. The SDK needs an explicit durable execution/enqueue/redrive contract or a host-supplied durable dispatcher/outbox hook, plus a supported way to re-enter the ordinary downstream call-tool pipeline after restart.
candidate_contract.chat_native_boundary: A resident durable dispatcher/outbox is a useful open-source durability pattern but is not itself a zero-residual Chat-native executor; it introduces an execution service that must be accounted for separately.

counterexamples: Persisting only McpTaskInfo leaves CreateTaskAsync-success / Task.Run-not-scheduled unrecoverable.
Calling McpServerTool.InvokeAsync directly on redrive can bypass ordinary authorization/policy filters.
A claim generation prevents stale terminal-state writes but cannot prevent a stale attempt from duplicating a non-idempotent external effect after lease expiry.
Cancellation can invalidate later completion recording but does not retroactively stop an already-issued external effect.
A replay envelope with a mismatched intent/principal must not be adopted merely because the task ID matches.

executed_artifact.fixtures: Atomic task+outbox persistence, crash-before-schedule redrive, single active claim, takeover generation, stale completion rejection, cancellation fencing, effect idempotency positive, no-idempotency duplicate negative, full-pipeline authorization recheck, direct-primitive bypass negative, intent mismatch, terminal non-reclaim, and claim-not-effect-receipt.
